subject.name_or_desc: A sick person (the patient), asked about by others

context.question: If bewitched?
context.asked_at: Anno 1646 (figure heading fragment); the day is not legible in the OCR.
context.setting: The physicians had prescribed much physic and it wrought no effect, but the patient was worse and worse, which gave those that asked some reason to suspect witchcraft.

attachments.key_positions: The Moon going to an opposition of Saturn, both planets in the sixth and twelfth houses (which gave suspicion of witchcraft); but neither the Ascendant nor its lord, nor the Moon, afflicted by the lord of the twelfth; the Moon applying after her opposition of Saturn unto the lord of the Ascendant, he above the earth ascending towards the meridian; Saturn on the cusp of the sixth, its lady in the twelfth
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XCIV: if bewitched (printed pp.468–470)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
